# Jon Marius Vaag Iversen {.hero-title}

::: {.affiliation}
Research Professor, Centre for Economic Research (SØF), NTNU Social Research  
Associate Professor (part-time), Department of Economics, NTNU
:::

::: {.biography}
I am an applied economist with a PhD in economics from NTNU. My research focuses on the economics of education, with a particular interest in how assessment, school resources and the composition of classrooms affect students' achievement, educational choices and later labour market outcomes.

My work draws on administrative register data, experiments and applied econometric methods. Alongside my academic research, I lead and contribute to policy-oriented projects on education, labour markets and the financing and organisation of public services. At NTNU, I teach undergraduate statistics and econometrics.
:::

::: {.interest-tags}
Education economics · Labour economics · Applied microeconometrics · Public economics
:::

## Featured research

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
::: {.eyebrow}
Ongoing research programme · 2026–2029

### EduGAP: Grading, Assessment and Pathways

How do school assessment practices shape achievement, educational choices and later labour market outcomes? I lead this international collaboration between NTNU Social Research, NTNU, UCL and the University of Texas at Austin, funded by the Research Council of Norway (approximately NOK 12 million).

[Explore the project](projects.qmd)
:::
::: {.feature-card}
::: {.eyebrow}
Working paper · 2026
:::
### Exams as Information: Exposure to Math Exams and Later Study Choices

With Colin P. Green, Lindsey Macmillan and Gill Wyness. We study how exposure to mathematics examinations affects pupils’ later mathematics and STEM choices.

[See current working papers](research.qmd#current-working-papers)
